notes: What is within reach in a laid-out room, where you stand after walking up to something or stepping back from it, and the doctor's warning for a place with no layout. A room is a box in its parent's plane and a spot is a cell of it in that plane. A case is one of five asks. within: whether the spot to is within arm's length of from (the same cell or one of the eight around it). nearest_free: where you stand after walking from from up to target in room, with taken the cells others stand or lie in: the cell inside the walls within arm's length of target, not target's own and not taken (from always counts as free), fewest paces from from, ties to the first north to south then west to east; null when there is none. step_back: where you stand after stepping back from away at from in room: a cell inside the walls step_back_paces from from and step_back_paces farther from away than from was, the one whose larger axis from away is largest, ties to the first north to south then west to east; refused no_room_behind when there is none. nearest_within_reach: the index of the first of people within arm's length of from with the fewest paces to it, or null. findings: a story and every row its records hold (stories, locations); output is reach::findings, one warning room_without_a_layout for each of the story's places with neither a box (x, y, z, width, depth) nor a footprint (width and depth). No die is thrown.
